questions: Who was the first President of the United States?
Washington served as the first U.S. president from 1789 to 1797.
Which ancient civilisation built the pyramids at Giza?
The Giza pyramids were built by Egyptians during the Old Kingdom, around 2600–2500 BC.
In which year did World War II end?
World War II ended in 1945 with the surrender of Germany in May and Japan in September.
Which ship famously sank on its maiden voyage in 1912?
RMS Titanic struck an iceberg and sank in April 1912.
Who was the famous French military leader who became Emperor in 1804?
Napoleon crowned himself Emperor of the French in 1804.
Which wall divided the city of Berlin from 1961 to 1989?
The Berlin Wall separated East and West Berlin until it fell in November 1989.
Machu Picchu is a 15th-century Inca citadel in the Andes of Peru.
Who wrote the Declaration of Independence's first draft?
Jefferson was the principal author of the 1776 Declaration of Independence.
What were the ancient Egyptian kings called?
Rulers of ancient Egypt are known as pharaohs.
Which famous explorer sailed across the Atlantic in 1492?
Columbus reached the Caribbean in October 1492.
In which country did the Olympic Games originate?
The ancient Olympic Games were held at Olympia in Greece from 776 BC.
What was the name of the first artificial satellite, launched in 1957?
The Soviet Union launched Sputnik 1 on 4 October 1957.
Which empire was ruled by Julius Caesar's successors, starting with Augustus?
Augustus became the first Roman emperor in 27 BC.
In which year did the French Revolution begin?
The storming of the Bastille on 14 July 1789 is a symbol of the Revolution's start.
Who was the first woman to win a Nobel Prize?
Marie Curie shared the 1903 Nobel Prize in Physics.
Which English queen ruled for over 63 years in the 19th and early 20th centuries?
The Magna Carta was sealed by which English king in 1215?
King John agreed to the Magna Carta at Runnymede in 1215.
Which city was buried by the eruption of Mount Vesuvius in AD 79?
Pompeii and Herculaneum were buried under volcanic ash in AD 79.
Who was the leader of the Soviet Union during most of World War II?
Stalin led the USSR from the mid-1920s until his death in 1953.
Which explorer's expedition completed the first circumnavigation of the globe?
Magellan's expedition (1519–1522) completed the circumnavigation, though he died on the way.
What was the name of the trade route linking China with the Mediterranean?
The Silk Road was a network of routes connecting East Asia and the Mediterranean.
Which war was fought between the North and South regions of the United States from 1861 to 1865?
The Civil War was fought between the Union and the Confederacy.
Who was the British Prime Minister for most of World War II?
Churchill led the UK from May 1940 to July 1945.
Which ancient wonder stood in the harbour of Rhodes?
The Colossus of Rhodes was a giant bronze statue of the sun god Helios.
Who was the first person to walk on the Moon?
Neil Armstrong stepped onto the Moon on 20 July 1969.
Which civilisation developed the cuneiform writing system?
The Sumerians of Mesopotamia developed cuneiform around 3200 BC.
Which South African leader was imprisoned for 27 years before becoming president?
Mandela was released in 1990 and became president in 1994.
The Battle of Hastings took place in which year?
William of Normandy defeated King Harold II at Hastings in 1066.
Which Chinese dynasty began construction of what became the Great Wall under its first emperor?
Qin Shi Huang linked earlier walls; much of the surviving wall dates from the Ming.
Which document begins with the words 'We the People'?
The Preamble of the U.S. Constitution opens with 'We the People'.
Who was the Egyptian queen allied with Mark Antony?
Cleopatra VII allied with Mark Antony against Octavian.
Which country was the first to grant women the right to vote in national elections, in 1893?
New Zealand became the first self-governing country to give women the vote in 1893.
What was the name of the period of cultural rebirth in Europe from the 14th to 17th centuries?
The Renaissance began in Italy and revived classical learning and art.
Which Mongol leader founded the largest contiguous land empire in history?
Genghis Khan founded the Mongol Empire in 1206.
In which year did the Berlin Wall fall?
Which treaty formally ended World War I between Germany and the Allies?
The Treaty of Versailles was signed on 28 June 1919.
Which Byzantine emperor commissioned the Hagia Sophia that stands today?
Justinian I rebuilt the Hagia Sophia, completed in 537.
Who was the first emperor of a unified China?
Qin Shi Huang unified China in 221 BC.
The Rosetta Stone helped scholars decipher which writing system?
Its parallel Greek text allowed Champollion to decipher hieroglyphs in 1822.
Which empire was ruled from Constantinople after the fall of the Western Roman Empire?
The Eastern Roman (Byzantine) Empire lasted until 1453.
In which year did Constantinople fall to the Ottoman Turks?
Sultan Mehmed II captured Constantinople on 29 May 1453.
Which Carthaginian general crossed the Alps with elephants to invade Italy?
Hannibal crossed the Alps in 218 BC during the Second Punic War.
Who led the Haitian Revolution and is regarded as its foremost leader?
Toussaint Louverture led the revolt that ended slavery in Saint-Domingue.
Which Indian emperor converted to Buddhism after the bloody Kalinga War?
Ashoka of the Maurya Empire embraced Buddhism around 260 BC.
The Meiji Restoration of 1868 took place in which country?
The Meiji Restoration returned power to the Japanese emperor and began rapid modernisation.
Which city-state was famous for its militaristic society and warriors at Thermopylae?
King Leonidas led Spartans at Thermopylae in 480 BC.
Who was the first female Prime Minister of the United Kingdom?
Which plague pandemic killed a large share of Europe's population in the mid-14th century?
The Black Death peaked in Europe from 1347 to 1351.
The Aztec capital Tenochtitlan stood on the site of which modern city?
Mexico City was built over the ruins of Tenochtitlan.
Which Venetian merchant described his travels to Kublai Khan's court?
Marco Polo's travels were recorded in 'The Travels of Marco Polo'.
In which year did the Russian Revolution overthrow the Tsar?
The February Revolution of 1917 forced Tsar Nicholas II to abdicate.
Who was the first Roman emperor to convert to Christianity?
Constantine converted and legalised Christianity with the Edict of Milan in 313.
Which ancient city was the capital of the Persian Achaemenid Empire's ceremonial palaces?
Persepolis was founded by Darius I around 518 BC.
The Battle of Waterloo in 1815 took place in which present-day country?
Waterloo lies just south of Brussels in Belgium.
Which explorer led the first expedition to reach the South Pole, in 1911?
Amundsen's Norwegian team reached the pole on 14 December 1911.
Which medieval ruler was crowned Emperor of the Romans on Christmas Day in 800?
Pope Leo III crowned Charlemagne in Rome in 800.
The Hundred Years' War was fought mainly between England and which country?
Which civilisation built the city of Chichén Itzá?
Chichén Itzá was a major Maya city on the Yucatán Peninsula.
Which French heroine was burned at the stake in 1431?
Joan of Arc was executed in Rouen in 1431 and later canonised.
In which year did India gain independence from British rule?
What was the name of the 1962 confrontation between the United States and the Soviet Union over missiles in Cuba?
The 13-day standoff in October 1962 is known as the Cuban Missile Crisis.
Who was the Macedonian king who conquered the Persian Empire by 330 BC?
Alexander's campaigns created one of the largest empires of the ancient world.
Which ancient Greek historian is often called the 'Father of History'?
Herodotus wrote 'The Histories' in the 5th century BC.
